findings.detail: 11 cards flush against the left edge of table at rest (1px gap, e.g. th)
findings.name: Cards flush against the scroller edge
findings.description: Cards inside a horizontal scroller or tab panel sit flush against the container edge at rest while keeping a gutter on the other side, so their edges and rounded corners get cut off. Usually the panel is sized wider than its clip box. Keep a consistent inset on both sides.
findings.label: Cards flush against the scroller edge
Text occluded by an overlapping element

findings.detail: span.lx-transfer-panel__selected-name-full "历史授权单位（记录中）：跨区域应急联动研判与协同" is 91% covered by an opaque element (span.lx-transfer-panel__node-code)
findings.name: Text occluded by an overlapping element
findings.description: Text is painted under an opaque element or a second text run, so part of it cannot be read. A decorative box, a stacked layer, or an inline element with leaked padding lands on the words instead of beside them. Give overlapping layers room, or move the text out from under the layer above it.
findings.label: Text occluded by an overlapping element

findings.name: Bounce or elastic easing
findings.description: Bounce and elastic easing feel dated and tacky. Real objects decelerate smoothly — use exponential easing (ease-out-quart/quint/expo) instead.
findings.label: Bounce or elastic easing

findings.detail: transition: height, padding-top, padding-bottom
findings.name: Layout property animation
findings.description: Animating width, height, padding, or margin causes layout thrash and janky performance. Use transform and opacity instead, or grid-template-rows for height animations.
findings.label: Layout property animation

findings.name: Cramped padding
findings.description: Text is too close to the edge of its container. Two shapes: (1) an element with its own text where the padding is too low for the font size, and (2) a wrapper with text-bearing children and near-zero padding against a visible boundary (border, outline, or non-transparent background) — children land flush against the boundary line. Add at least 8px (ideally 12–16px) of padding inside bordered, outlined, or colored containers.
findings.label: Cramped padding

findings.detail: 11 cards flush against the left edge of table at rest (1px gap, e.g. th)
findings.name: Cards flush against the scroller edge
findings.description: Cards inside a horizontal scroller or tab panel sit flush against the container edge at rest while keeping a gutter on the other side, so their edges and rounded corners get cut off. Usually the panel is sized wider than its clip box. Keep a consistent inset on both sides.
findings.label: Cards flush against the scroller edge

findings.detail: span.lx-transfer-panel__selected-name-full "历史授权单位（记录中）：跨区域应急联动研判与协同" is 91% covered by an opaque element (span.lx-transfer-panel__node-code)
findings.name: Text occluded by an overlapping element
findings.description: Text is painted under an opaque element or a second text run, so part of it cannot be read. A decorative box, a stacked layer, or an inline element with leaked padding lands on the words instead of beside them. Give overlapping layers room, or move the text out from under the layer above it.
findings.label: Text occluded by an overlapping element

findings.name: Bounce or elastic easing
findings.description: Bounce and elastic easing feel dated and tacky. Real objects decelerate smoothly — use exponential easing (ease-out-quart/quint/expo) instead.
findings.label: Bounce or elastic easing

findings.detail: transition: height, padding-top, padding-bottom
findings.name: Layout property animation
findings.description: Animating width, height, padding, or margin causes layout thrash and janky performance. Use transform and opacity instead, or grid-template-rows for height animations.
findings.label: Layout property animation

findings.label: Positioned child clipped by overflow container

findings.detail: span.container clips a positioned child
findings.name: Positioned child clipped by overflow container
findings.description: A clipping container (overflow hidden or clip) wrapping an absolutely-positioned child cuts off tooltips, menus, and popovers that need to escape. Let the overflow be visible, or move the positioned layer out of the clip.
findings.label: Positioned child clipped by overflow container

findings.detail: <div> "transfer-panel-demo__preview": children flush against bg on right/bottom/left (no inset)
findings.name: Cramped padding
findings.description: Text is too close to the edge of its container. Two shapes: (1) an element with its own text where the padding is too low for the font size, and (2) a wrapper with text-bearing children and near-zero padding against a visible boundary (border, outline, or non-transparent background) — children land flush against the boundary line. Add at least 8px (ideally 12–16px) of padding inside bordered, outlined, or colored containers.
findings.label: Cramped padding

findings.detail: raster background at opacity 0
findings.name: Raster buried under a wash or opacity
findings.description: A background image under a near-opaque gradient wash, or a raster on an element at near-zero opacity, never reaches the screen: the page shows the wash, and the produced texture or photo ships as a compliance token. Let the material show (a tint under 0.9 alpha, a blend mode, an opacity you can see) or remove the file.
findings.label: Raster buried under a wash or opacity

findings.detail: 11 cards flush against the left edge of table at rest (1px gap, e.g. th)
findings.name: Cards flush against the scroller edge
findings.description: Cards inside a horizontal scroller or tab panel sit flush against the container edge at rest while keeping a gutter on the other side, so their edges and rounded corners get cut off. Usually the panel is sized wider than its clip box. Keep a consistent inset on both sides.
findings.label: Cards flush against the scroller edge

findings.name: Bounce or elastic easing
findings.description: Bounce and elastic easing feel dated and tacky. Real objects decelerate smoothly — use exponential easing (ease-out-quart/quint/expo) instead.
findings.label: Bounce or elastic easing

findings.detail: transition: height, padding-top, padding-bottom
findings.name: Layout property animation
findings.description: Animating width, height, padding, or margin causes layout thrash and janky performance. Use transform and opacity instead, or grid-template-rows for height animations.
findings.label: Layout property animation

findings.detail: span.container clips a positioned child
findings.name: Positioned child clipped by overflow container
findings.description: A clipping container (overflow hidden or clip) wrapping an absolutely-positioned child cuts off tooltips, menus, and popovers that need to escape. Let the overflow be visible, or move the positioned layer out of the clip.
findings.label: Positioned child clipped by overflow container

findings.label: Positioned child clipped by overflow container

findings.detail: span.container clips a positioned child
findings.name: Positioned child clipped by overflow container
findings.description: A clipping container (overflow hidden or clip) wrapping an absolutely-positioned child cuts off tooltips, menus, and popovers that need to escape. Let the overflow be visible, or move the positioned layer out of the clip.
findings.label: Positioned child clipped by overflow container

findings.detail: <div> "transfer-panel-demo__preview": children flush against bg on right/bottom/left (no inset)
findings.name: Cramped padding
findings.description: Text is too close to the edge of its container. Two shapes: (1) an element with its own text where the padding is too low for the font size, and (2) a wrapper with text-bearing children and near-zero padding against a visible boundary (border, outline, or non-transparent background) — children land flush against the boundary line. Add at least 8px (ideally 12–16px) of padding inside bordered, outlined, or colored containers.
findings.label: Cramped padding

Cards flush against the scroller edge

findings.detail: 30 cards flush against the right edge of table at rest (-13px gap, e.g. th)
findings.name: Cards flush against the scroller edge
findings.description: Cards inside a horizontal scroller or tab panel sit flush against the container edge at rest while keeping a gutter on the other side, so their edges and rounded corners get cut off. Usually the panel is sized wider than its clip box. Keep a consistent inset on both sides.
findings.label: Cards flush against the scroller edge
Text occluded by an overlapping element

findings.detail: span.lang "vue" is 50% covered by overlapping text (p)
findings.name: Text occluded by an overlapping element
findings.description: Text is painted under an opaque element or a second text run, so part of it cannot be read. A decorative box, a stacked layer, or an inline element with leaked padding lands on the words instead of beside them. Give overlapping layers room, or move the text out from under the layer above it.
findings.label: Text occluded by an overlapping element

findings.detail: transition: height, padding-top, padding-bottom
findings.name: Layout property animation
findings.description: Animating width, height, padding, or margin causes layout thrash and janky performance. Use transform and opacity instead, or grid-template-rows for height animations.
findings.label: Layout property animation

findings.name: Text occluded by an overlapping element

Give overlapping layers room, or move the text out from under the layer above it.
findings.label: Text occluded by an overlapping element

findings.label: Layout property animation

findings.label: Positioned child clipped by overflow container

findings.detail: span.container clips a positioned child
findings.name: Positioned child clipped by overflow container
findings.description: A clipping container (overflow hidden or clip) wrapping an absolutely-positioned child cuts off tooltips, menus, and popovers that need to escape. Let the overflow be visible, or move the positioned layer out of the clip.
findings.label: Positioned child clipped by overflow container

findings.detail: <div> "virtual-tree-demo__preview": children flush against bg on right/bottom/left (no inset)
findings.name: Cramped padding
findings.description: Text is too close to the edge of its container. Two shapes: (1) an element with its own text where the padding is too low for the font size, and (2) a wrapper with text-bearing children and near-zero padding against a visible boundary (border, outline, or non-transparent background) — children land flush against the boundary line. Add at least 8px (ideally 12–16px) of padding inside bordered, outlined, or colored containers.
findings.label: Cramped padding

findings.detail: raster background at opacity 0
findings.name: Raster buried under a wash or opacity
findings.description: A background image under a near-opaque gradient wash, or a raster on an element at near-zero opacity, never reaches the screen: the page shows the wash, and the produced texture or photo ships as a compliance token. Let the material show (a tint under 0.9 alpha, a blend mode, an opacity you can see) or remove the file.
findings.label: Raster buried under a wash or opacity

findings.description: Text does not meet WCAG AA contrast requirements (4.5:1 for body, 3:1 for large text). Increase the contrast between text and background.
findings.label: Low contrast text

findings.detail: raster background at opacity 0
findings.name: Raster buried under a wash or opacity
findings.description: A background image under a near-opaque gradient wash, or a raster on an element at near-zero opacity, never reaches the screen: the page shows the wash, and the produced texture or photo ships as a compliance token. Let the material show (a tint under 0.9 alpha, a blend mode, an opacity you can see) or remove the file.
findings.label: Raster buried under a wash or opacity

findings.detail: <div> "virtual-tree-demo__preview": children flush against bg on right/bottom/left (no inset)
findings.name: Cramped padding
findings.description: Text is too close to the edge of its container. Two shapes: (1) an element with its own text where the padding is too low for the font size, and (2) a wrapper with text-bearing children and near-zero padding against a visible boundary (border, outline, or non-transparent background) — children land flush against the boundary line. Add at least 8px (ideally 12–16px) of padding inside bordered, outlined, or colored containers.
findings.label: Cramped padding
